stem: Bobby cared a lot about his ____ at home and asked his parents not to go through his things without his permission.
explain_zh: Bobby很在意在家裡的「隱私」，要求父母不要未經許可翻動他的東西，故選 privacy。discipline 指「紀律」、facility 指「設施」、representation 指「代表」，皆與「個人空間不被侵犯」的語意無關。privacy 常用於描述個人隱私權。

stem: The new manager is a real gentleman. He is kind and humble, totally different from the former manager, who was ____ and bossy.
explain_zh: 新來的經理待人謙和有禮，與前任經理「刻薄」又愛使喚人的作風截然不同，故選 mean，在此作形容詞指「刻薄的」。eager（渴望的）、liberal（開明的）、inferior（低劣的）皆無法與 bossy 並列形容令人不悅的個性。mean 常用來形容待人苛刻小氣。

stem: The weather bureau ____ that the typhoon would bring strong winds and heavy rains, and warned everyone of the possible danger.
explain_zh: 氣象局「預測」颱風將帶來強風豪雨，並提醒民眾注意可能的危險，故選 predicted。conveyed（傳達）、associated（使有關聯）、interpreted（詮釋）皆無法表達「根據氣象資料推測未來」的語意。predict 常用於天氣或趨勢的預測。

stem: Different airlines have different ____ for carry-on luggage, but many international airlines limit a carry-on piece to 7 kilograms.
explain_zh: 不同航空公司對手提行李有不同的「限制」，但許多國際航班將手提行李限重在七公斤，故選 restrictions。landmarks（地標）、percentages（百分比）、circumstances（情況）皆無法形容行李規範。restriction 常用於描述規則上的限制。

stem: Many people were happy that the government had finally ____ Children's Day as a national holiday.
explain_zh: 政府終於「宣布」將兒童節訂為國定假日，讓許多人感到開心，故選 declared。appointed（指派）、performed（表演、執行）、involved（涉及）皆無法與 Children's Day as a national holiday 搭配出「宣布訂定」的語意。declare 常用於正式宣告某項決定。

stem: To reach the goal of making her company a market leader, Michelle ____ a plan to open ten new stores around the country this year.
explain_zh: 為了讓公司成為市場領導者，蜜雪兒「提出」今年在全國展店十家的計畫，故選 proposed。advised（建議）、occupied（占據）、recognized（認出、認可）皆無法與 a plan 搭配出「提出計畫」的語意。propose 常用於提案或倡議。

stem: Silence in some way is as ____ as speech. It can be used to show, for example, disagreement or lack of interest.
explain_zh: 沉默在某種程度上和說話一樣「富有表達力」，可以用來展現不同意或缺乏興趣，故選 expressive。sociable（善於社交的）、reasonable（合理的）、objective（客觀的）皆無法形容「沉默也能傳達訊息」的特質。expressive 常用來形容能有效傳達情感或意涵。

stem: This TV program is designed for children, ____ for those under five. It contains no violence or strong language.
explain_zh: 這個電視節目是為兒童設計的，「特別是」為五歲以下的孩子設計，故選 particularly。sensibly（明智地）、moderately（適度地）、considerably（相當地）皆無法表達「特別針對某族群」的語意。particularly 常用於強調特定對象或情況。

stem: Tommy, please put away the toys in the box, or you might ____ on them and hurt yourself.
explain_zh: 叫湯米把玩具收進箱子，不然可能會「絆倒」而受傷，故選 stumble。graze（擦傷、放牧）、navigate（導航）、dwell（居住）皆無法形容「被物品絆倒」的動作。stumble on/over 是常見的固定搭配。

stem: The ____ costume party, held every September, is one of the biggest events of the school year.
explain_zh: 每年九月舉辦的「年度」變裝派對是這學年最盛大的活動之一，故選 annual。initial（最初的）、evident（明顯的）、occasional（偶爾的）皆無法形容「每年固定舉行」的活動。annual event 是常見的固定搭配。

stem: In a job interview, attitude and personality are usually important ____ that influence the decision of the interviewers.
explain_zh: 求職面試中，態度與個性通常是影響面試官決定的重要「因素」，故選 factors。outcomes（結果）、missions（任務）、identities（身分）皆無法形容「影響決定的要素」。factor 常用於描述影響結果的關鍵條件。

stem: The snow-capped mountain is described so ____ in the book that the scene seems to come alive in front of the reader's eyes.
explain_zh: 書中把白雪皚皚的山描述得如此「生動」，使場景彷彿在讀者眼前活了過來，故選 vividly。distantly（疏遠地）、meaningfully（有意義地）、cheerfully（愉快地）皆無法形容「描寫得栩栩如生」的效果。vividly 常用於描述文字或畫面的生動程度。

stem: Surrounded by flowers blooming and birds ____ merrily, the Wangs had a good time hiking in the national park.
explain_zh: 在盛開的花朵與「啁啾」鳴叫的鳥兒圍繞下，王家一行人在國家公園健行得很愉快，故選 chirping。napping（打盹）、scooping（舀取）、flipping（翻轉）皆無法形容鳥類的叫聲。chirp 專指鳥類清脆的鳴叫聲。

stem: It is essential for us to maintain constant ____ with our friends to ensure that we have someone to talk to in times of need.
explain_zh: 與朋友保持恆常的「聯繫」，才能確保需要時有人可以傾訴，故選 contact。benefit（利益）、gesture（手勢）、favor（幫忙）皆無法與 maintain 搭配出「保持聯絡」的語意。maintain contact with 是常見的固定搭配。

stem: The young generation in this country has shown less interest in factory work and other ____ labor jobs, such as house construction and fruit picking.
explain_zh: 現在年輕世代對工廠工作及其他「勞力」工作（如房屋營建、水果採收）的興趣降低，故選 manual。causal（因果的）、durable（耐用的）、violent（暴力的）皆無法形容以體力勞動為主的工作性質。manual labor 是常見的固定搭配，指體力勞動。

A camera and a viewing system are built (26) these glasses. As the wearer brings the food toward their mouth, the camera captures an image of the food. It replays the image back through the glasses after processing it on an attached computer. The size of the food they are about to eat is magnified while (27) of their hand remains normal. Their brain is (28) tricked into thinking they are eating more than they really are. The study showed that participants who wore the glasses ate 9.3% less than those who did not wear them.
The team has also developed a special device which uses scent bottles and visual trickery to make the wearers of these glasses think that the plain snack they are eating is (29) than it actually is. The device, for instance, can be set to (30) one's favorite flavor. Recent experiments with this device showed that 80% of the participants were fooled by the smell. For example, some participants thought that they were eating a chocolate snack, but in fact they were not.
stem: (29) 應填入：The wearers of these glasses think that the plain snack they are eating is ____ than it actually is.
explain_zh: 這項裝置利用氣味瓶與視覺錯覺，讓配戴者以為自己吃的平淡零食「更美味」，故選 tastier。prettier（更漂亮）、larger（更大）、healthier（更健康）皆與「氣味影響味覺感受」的語境不符。

passage:
Angelfish, often found in the warm seas and coral reefs, are among the most brightly colored fish of the ocean. Brilliant colors and stripes form amazing patterns on their body. These patterns actually help the fish to hide from danger among roots and plants. At night, when these fish become inactive, their colors may become pale. Often, the young ones are differently colored than the adults. Some scientists believe that the color difference between the young and the old indicates their different social positions.
Another interesting fact about angelfish is that they have an occupation in the fish world. Most of them act as cleaners for other fish and pick dead tissue from their bodies. This is not their food, though. Their diet consists mainly of sponge and algae.
One particular kind of angelfish, the blackspot angelfish, has a special capability that allows it to change gender from female to male. However, the change is not made at random; it happens for a specific reason. Angelfish live in groups, and each group has one male fish, which is blue in color, and four female fish, which are yellow. The male angelfish is the strongest and largest member of the group. He is the one who protects and looks after the females. When the male dies, the group needs a new “security guard.” This is when the largest female in the group begins to change in appearance. She begins to grow larger in size, and after a week, she starts changing color, from yellow to blue. Slowly, her behavior toward the other fish also changes. She begins behaving like a male. Two weeks later, black stripes appear on her body, indicating the gender change is complete. She is now completely male!
stem: What is the job of an angelfish in the sea?
options: Being a cleaner for other fish.
Being a bodyguard for other fish.
Being a gardener for roots and plants.
Being a caretaker for sponge and algae.
explain_zh: 天使魚在海洋世界中的職業是幫其他魚類清除身上的死亡組織，扮演「清潔工」的角色，故選 A。B、C、D 皆與文中描述的實際工作內容不符，牠們並非保鑣、園丁或照顧者。

passage:
Totem poles in North America are poles or posts carved with symbols or figures by Aboriginal peoples of the Northwest Coast. Carved from large, straight trees and painted vibrant colors, the totem poles are not just unique works of art. The coastal peoples have long passed on knowledge from generation to generation through oral traditions, and totem poles were the traditional way of telling the story of an individual family or clan.
The totem pole can be grouped into specific categories, depending on its location and the occasion for which it was carved. Welcome poles were traditionally placed on village beachfronts to greet visitors arriving by canoe. Inside the homes of high-ranking chiefs is where house poles were found. The family's history was carefully carved into each pole. Placed along the rear or front walls of a house, house poles also helped to support the main beam of the roof.
Memorial poles stood in front of a house. They were erected in memory of a deceased chief or a high-ranking clan member. The poles depicted the person's accomplishments or family history. Mortuary poles were also raised to honor the dead, but they differed from memorial poles, having a burial box placed at the top of the pole. Inside the burial box were the remains of the deceased.
While many of these poles can still be found in various locations on the west coast of North America, there is one pole that can now only be found in a museum—the shame pole. Traditionally, shame poles were carved for a chief to embarrass and ridicule another who had done something wrong. Once the wrong was made right, the pole was taken down.
Totem poles are important expressions of specific Aboriginal cultures. Despite the threats posed by cultural and political encroachment of colonial forces, the art of totem pole carving has survived. Aboriginal carvers continue to carve totems as symbols of their cultural pride and clan kinship.
stem: Which of the following is the best title for this passage?
options: Totem Poles, the Legends of Aboriginal Peoples

explain_zh: 全文依序介紹迎賓柱、家柱、紀念柱、墓葬柱及恥辱柱等不同類型圖騰柱各自的「功能」，最適合的標題是 Totem Poles: Their Functions，故選 B。選項 A、C、D 皆只涵蓋部分內容，並非全文核心。

passage:
Music has a tendency to get stuck in our heads. Sometimes a tune intrudes on our thoughts and then plays, and replays, in a never-ending loop. This interesting phenomenon becomes a subject explored by many scientists. They use a range of terms to describe it—stuck-song syndrome, sticky music, cognitive itch, or most commonly “earworm.” Earworms can run around our heads for several minutes to numerous hours. As the melody repeats, it becomes embedded into our mind. Even though our ears do not hear the tune, our brain continues to play it.
Earworms often take the form of song fragments rather than entire songs, and the song is usually a familiar one. Researchers are not sure why some songs are more likely to get stuck in our heads than others, but everyone has their own tunes. Often those songs have a simple, upbeat melody and catchy, repetitive lyrics, such as popular commercial jingles and slightly annoying radio hits. Recent or repeated exposure to a song or even a small part of a song can also trigger earworms, as can word associations, such as a phrase similar to the lyrics of a song.
While earworms might be annoying, most people who experience them nevertheless report that they are pleasant or at least neutral. Only a third of people are disturbed by the song in their heads. How people cope with their earworms seems to depend on how they feel about them. Those who have positive feelings about their stuck songs prefer to just “let them be,” while those with negative feelings turn to more behavioral responses, which include coping strategies such as singing, talking, or even praying.
stem: According to the passage, which of the following is true about an earworm?
options: It is a creature living inside our ears.
It is a tune memorized in a personal way.
It is a melody repeating in our heads.
It is a commercial recalled through lyrics.
explain_zh: 文中定義耳蟲現象是指旋律在腦海中「不斷重複播放」，故選 C。選項 A 誇張成「活在耳朵裡的生物」、B、D 皆非正確定義，屬於望文生義的陷阱選項。

passage:
Got a bug bite problem? Many people who are troubled by skin rashes caused by bug bites use “foggers,” or “bug bombs,” to get rid of the annoying crawlers in their homes. Many people think these bug killers or pesticides will penetrate every place where the insects hide. Actually, quite the opposite is true. Once the pests detect the chemical fog in the room, they'll hide themselves in walls or other hideaways, where you'll never be able to treat them effectively.
Ohio State University researchers tested three commercially sold foggers in a study on the effect of foggers on bedbugs. After testing these brands on five different groups of live bedbugs for two hours, the scientists saw that the foggers had little—if any—effect on the insects. The researchers said bedbugs hide in cracks and crevices such as under sheets and mattresses, or deep in carpets where foggers won't reach. Moreover, bugs that do come in contact with the mist may be resistant to the pesticide.
Foggers, or bug bombs, should really be a measure of last resort. First of all, the gases used in bug bombs are highly flammable and thus pose a serious risk of fire or explosion if the product is not used properly. Second, once a bug bomb is used, every surface in your home will be covered with the toxic pesticide. When you use a bug bomb, a chemical mixture rains down on your counters, furniture, floors, and walls, leaving behind oily and toxic substances. Your health might thus be endangered. Therefore, it is suggested that people leave the problem to the professionals.
stem: What is this passage mainly about?
options: Steps to get rid of bedbugs.
explain_zh: 全文說明煙霧殺蟲劑對床蝨等害蟲「效果不彰」，反而可能造成火災與健康風險，主軸是「殺蟲彈的無效性」，故選 C。選項 A、B、D 皆只涵蓋部分內容，並非全文核心。

passage:
Got a bug bite problem? Many people who are troubled by skin rashes caused by bug bites use “foggers,” or “bug bombs,” to get rid of the annoying crawlers in their homes. Many people think these bug killers or pesticides will penetrate every place where the insects hide. Actually, quite the opposite is true. Once the pests detect the chemical fog in the room, they'll hide themselves in walls or other hideaways, where you'll never be able to treat them effectively.
Ohio State University researchers tested three commercially sold foggers in a study on the effect of foggers on bedbugs. After testing these brands on five different groups of live bedbugs for two hours, the scientists saw that the foggers had little—if any—effect on the insects. The researchers said bedbugs hide in cracks and crevices such as under sheets and mattresses, or deep in carpets where foggers won't reach. Moreover, bugs that do come in contact with the mist may be resistant to the pesticide.
Foggers, or bug bombs, should really be a measure of last resort. First of all, the gases used in bug bombs are highly flammable and thus pose a serious risk of fire or explosion if the product is not used properly. Second, once a bug bomb is used, every surface in your home will be covered with the toxic pesticide. When you use a bug bomb, a chemical mixture rains down on your counters, furniture, floors, and walls, leaving behind oily and toxic substances. Your health might thus be endangered. Therefore, it is suggested that people leave the problem to the professionals.
